knowledge_graph.title: Collective trust fund
knowledge_graph.description: Collective trust funds or Collective Investment Trusts are a legal trust administered by a bank or trust company that combines assets for multiple investors who meet specific requirements set forth in the fund's declaration of trust.

text_blocks.snippet: A collective investment trust (CIT) is a pooled investment vehicle, similar to a mutual fund, but specifically designed for and only available to qualified retirement plans like 401(k)s and governmental plans. CITs are sponsored by banks or trust companies and are not subject to the same regulations as mutual funds, often resulting in lower fees and greater flexibility.

list.title: Pooled Investment Vehicle:
list.snippet: CITs combine the assets of multiple retirement plans, allowing them to access investments that might be difficult or expensive to acquire individually.

list.title: Qualified Retirement Plans:
list.snippet: CITs are exclusively for qualified retirement plans, such as 401(k)s, 403(b)s, and governmental plans.
